observations.statement: The document claims ownership of the operational migration from bootstrap planning files to canonical Plan documents and later native planning services, including trigger, phase, prompt, conversion, seal, and retired-experiment behavior.

The migration principles treat the bootstrap ledger as planning/source memory, reserve compilation for an explicit request from Jared, require pilot-first controlled conversion, delay indexing until source documents are stable enough, and reserve governance refresh for an explicit seal phase.

BPM-001 makes Root AGENTS.md the trigger and read/write-rule surface and names start, continue, compile, standardize, index, readiness, and seal triggers, with manual review and a ledger workflow smoke test as validation surfaces.
BPM-002 separates ordinary conversational ledger work from Goal Mode transformation phases and sets a less-than-4,000-character prompt target when possible.

BPM-003 requires initial compilation into four named owner documents plus Plans index registration before broader Plan conversion, and names existence, routing, lineage separation, and two repository commands as acceptance or validation surfaces.

BPM-004 defines lossless conversion as an inventory-and-proof sequence using hashes, span maps, coverage maps, ContractRefs, anchors or aliases, dispositions, a pilot, validators, and controlled batches; deletion or semantic change without source coverage stops migration.
Conversion ownership is split: Plan_Document_System owns conversion proof, while Bootstrap_Planning_Migration owns sequencing and pilot choice.

BPM-005 permits governance-artifact refresh only in an explicit seal phase after document and index churn stops, prohibits such refresh during ordinary planning phases, and prohibits WorkNodes or executable build tasks during indexing.
BPM-006 marks retired transfer experiments as source-lineage only and permits historical terms only as stale or retired lineage or negative constraints.

BPM-007 permits separate threads, requires each phase to start from a ledger ID, compact state, and canonical owner documents, and requires each phase to end with updated handoff state, validator reporting, and an exact next safe action.
The compilation coverage explicitly leaves the representative pilot choice to a later inventory phase and assigns neighboring conversion-proof and index/readiness ownership to other PlanUnits.

BPM-008 requires bounded read-only parallel subagents after atom, owner, or document thresholds are crossed, assignment/result evidence, blocking instead of silent single-agent execution, and a sole-writer main agent; it applies parallel review to multiple named deep-audit dimensions.

The BPM-008 repair behavior limits its closure matrix and closure-registry updates to actionable repair_required findings, uses bounded read-only specialists, no-ops when no actionable rows exist, and rejects passing validators as sufficient while actionable rows remain open.

The addenda repeatedly exclude WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, GoalRuns, implementation files, runtime artifacts, production build tasks, and buildability claims from this compile and hygiene scope.

The July 8 addendum characterizes this document as migration/source-lineage for an early workflow, assigns current live behavior to named current owner surfaces, and establishes that contradictions resolve in favor of those surfaces.

candidate_findings.title: Current authority is not resolved at clause level
candidate_findings.statement: The core first claims ownership of current bootstrap-ledger and migration behavior, but later characterizes the document as migration/source-lineage for an early workflow and redirects current behavior to other owner surfaces. It provides a precedence rule but no clause-level retirement or replacement map for BPM-001 through BPM-008, while explicitly recording that the workflow appears superseded and remains deferred.
candidate_findings.impact: An agent or builder cannot deterministically tell which accepted requirements in this document remain operative versus historical, risking execution of superseded workflow or silent omission of still-valid migration constraints.

candidate_findings.title: Indexing and seal transition criteria are undefined
candidate_findings.statement: The entry conditions use 'stable enough to index,' 'stop changing,' 'churn stops,' and 'stabilize' without a measurable snapshot, observation interval, approving authority, or required evidence bundle that establishes either transition.
candidate_findings.impact: Different operators can index or seal at different times, causing premature governance refresh, stale generated artifacts, or indefinite blocking.

candidate_findings.title: Mandatory parallel gate lacks executable thresholds and evidence contract
candidate_findings.statement: BPM-008 requires parallel subagents when atom, owner, or document thresholds are exceeded and requires assignment/result evidence, but this core supplies no threshold values, counting rules, evidence schema, minimum concurrency, or behavior when sufficient subagents are unavailable.
candidate_findings.impact: The mandatory gate cannot be applied deterministically or audited consistently, and an implementation may silently under-shard, over-shard, or block without a defined recovery path.

candidate_findings.title: Lossless conversion has no semantic completeness oracle
candidate_findings.statement: BPM-004 lists inventories, hashes, spans, coverage maps, preservation targets, and validators, and says uncovered deletion or semantic change stops migration, but it does not define coverage-map structure, semantic equivalence, required coverage completeness, disposition states, or who adjudicates disputed equivalence across the split owners.
candidate_findings.impact: A conversion may pass structural checks while losing meaning, or halt indefinitely because proof sufficiency and adjudication are left to consequential builder discretion.

candidate_findings.title: Representative pilot selection is nondeterministic
candidate_findings.statement: The pilot is only described as 'likely' a substantial owner/consumer document rather than a tiny addendum, and its actual choice is deferred to inventory; no ranking, tie-breaker, risk coverage, approval, or rejection rule is stated.
candidate_findings.impact: Different operators can choose materially different pilots, weakening the pilot's ability to validate the broad migration before rewrites begin.

candidate_findings.title: Goal Mode obligation has inconsistent normative strength
candidate_findings.statement: BPM-002 says transformation phases 'use Goal Mode,' while BPM-007 says they 'should use' compact Goal prompts; the prompt-size target is also qualified by 'when possible' without a required fallback when the limit cannot be met.
candidate_findings.impact: Phase behavior and prompt packaging can vary by operator, undermining independent thread restartability and consistent evidence production.

candidate_findings.title: Phase handoff omits failure, concurrency, and replay semantics
candidate_findings.statement: BPM-007 names phase inputs and outputs and a handoff path, but does not specify required handoff fields, validation of missing or corrupt compact state, behavior after validator failure, conflict handling when separate threads update one ledger, or idempotent replay of a partially completed phase.
candidate_findings.impact: Thread restarts can consume incomplete state, overwrite concurrent progress, repeat transformations, or advertise an unsafe next action without a deterministic recovery protocol.

candidate_findings.title: Repair adjudication and closure evidence are underspecified
candidate_findings.statement: The repair Goal may 'repair or adjudicate' actionable findings and update a semantic closure registry, but the core does not define adjudication authority, permissible closure dispositions, required evidence, atomic update behavior, or reconciliation when validators pass but a repair_required row remains open.
candidate_findings.impact: Actionable rows may be closed without adequate proof, remain inconsistently represented between the matrix and registry, or be repeatedly processed on reruns.

candidate_findings.title: Runtime-contract completion has no acceptance oracle
candidate_findings.statement: The governance behavior preserves runtime-disabled readiness unless runtime contracts were 'explicitly completed,' but the core does not identify the contract set, completion authority, evidence form, or state transition that proves completion; the addendum separately disclaims runtime and buildability proof.
candidate_findings.impact: A seal implementation could enable runtime readiness prematurely or keep it disabled after legitimate completion, directly affecting buildability truth.

candidate_findings.title: Validator surfaces do not define result semantics
candidate_findings.statement: The core names manual review, commands, reports, and inventories as validation surfaces but does not state required exit outcomes, report schemas, evidence retention, mapping from each result to acceptance criteria, or whether and how each failure blocks or rolls back a phase.
candidate_findings.impact: The same validator output can be interpreted differently across compile, migration, indexing, and seal phases, reducing reproducibility of acceptance decisions.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: Compilation authority is explicit: the bootstrap ledger is planning/source memory and compilation occurs only when Jared explicitly asks.
The core explicitly separates ledger source lineage from canonical Plan prose in trigger, initial compilation, and addendum acceptance behavior.
The scope boundary explicitly prohibits WorkNodes and executable build tasks during indexing and prohibits runtime or implementation artifacts during the ledger-to-Plans compile.
Parallel-work write authority is explicit: subagents are bounded and read-only and the main agent remains the sole writer.
The empty repair case and one insufficiency condition are explicit: repair no-ops with no actionable rows, while passing validators cannot close remaining repair_required rows.
A contradiction precedence rule is explicit: the named current owner documents and v2 state files win over this early-workflow migration/source-lineage document.
BPM-008 explicitly classifies its workflow behavior as non-GUI and explains that it concerns backend, planning, contract, governance, or workflow behavior rather than visual presentation.
The July 8 hygiene note explicitly declines to mark buildability true and states that no runtime or buildability proof is claimed for the deferred row.

unknowns.statement: Because the named current owner documents and v2 state files are outside this blind window, the actual current behavior, exact contradictions, and whether any supersession mapping exists there are unknown.
The actual representative pilot document has not been selected in this core and remains unknown.
No validator execution results or governance seal report are present in this core, so current validation and seal status are unknown.
Whether the named implementation surfaces define the omitted parallel thresholds, evidence schemas, and resource-failure behavior cannot be determined from this window.
The identity and completion state of the runtime contracts referenced by the readiness guard are unknown in this core.
The existence, validity, and current contents of any ledger handoff state are unknown; the core names only the path and phase-level expectations.
Cancellation, retry limits, partial-batch recovery, and idempotency behavior for migration, audit, repair, and seal operations are not stated in this core.
